items.item: Builds anticipation/dread before reveal (cues, telegraphs) rather than leading with a jump scare
Addresses that groups of friends reduce fear (separation mechanics or per-player experiences)
Has a readable threat language players can learn and counterplay
Includes tension/release pacing and recovery after the encounter
Considers Roblox constraints (mobile brightness/readability, client-local effects, audio)
Is specific to the hospital setting rather than generic

slop: The 'Anti-slop check' table and the 'Apex' header are meta process notes that don't help the design
A 40% random chance of checking the player's hiding spot undermines the readable, learnable threat
Scripted ceiling-tile noise forces the first chase instead of it coming from player mistakes
Concrete speed and radius numbers are presented as settled values with no reasoning
overengineering: The noise-radius scaling formula and per-player-count patrol speeds are premature for a first-encounter design

raw.reason: A forces the group to split with a two-location objective, lets one player see a scare the others don't, and makes the call-bell lure a real co-op choice. Its threat rules are fully learnable and closely tied to the hospital. B has more useful Roblox implementation notes, but it only partly handles group separation, adds randomness that hurts readability, and never covers mobile readability.
